name: SLOVENIA

flag.title: Flag of Slovenia
flag.note: Blue, white & red with Triglav crest

lead: Slovenia is a small country with Alpine peaks, turquoise rivers and ancient caves. It is smaller than Wales. You can drive from snowy mountains to an Adriatic beach in under two hours. About 2 million people live here. The capital, Ljubljana, sits under a hilltop castle.

geo: Slovenia packs four landscapes into one small country. The Julian Alps have jagged peaks in the north-west. The Soča River runs neon blue.
More than 58% of Slovenia is forest. Its Adriatic coast is only 47 km long, with the old town of Piran.
animals: Around 1,000 brown bears roam the Kočevje forests in the south. That is one of Europe's densest bear groups. Lynx and grey wolves live here too.
The olm is a blind, pale salamander found only in Karst caves. It survives ten years without food. The fat dormouse was once hunted at harvest time.
culture: Many Slovenians keep bees. The Carniolan bee is a protected symbol. Farmers paint beehive panels, called panjske končnice, with folk art. UNESCO lists Slovenia's beekeeping tradition.
Food is hearty mountain fare: žlikrofi dumplings, štruklji pastry and potica, a walnut-spiral cake for every celebration.
history: Roman roads crossed Slovenia 2,000 years ago. By 14 AD, the city of Emona, today's Ljubljana, was busy. Slavic tribes arrived in the 6th century.
After World War I, Slovenia joined Yugoslavia. It became independent on 25 June 1991, after a ten-day war. It joined NATO and the EU in 2004, then the Euro in 2007.
wows: Slovenia is the only country with 'love' in its name (Slo-LOVE-nia).
Postojna Cave has its own railway, with tiny electric trains since 1872.
The blind olm can live over 100 years.
Slovenia has more than 14,000 caves, one of Earth's highest cave densities per km².
The Soča River glows turquoise, visible from the hills above.
Ljubljana's historic core went car-free in 2007, so locals walk or cycle.
Slovenia gave the UN World Bee Day, 20 May, birthday of Anton Janša.

myths.myth: Slovenia and Slovakia are the same place
myths.fact: They are two countries. Slovakia lies farther east and has no coast. Their flags look alike.
Dormice are not true mice. They are their own family, and sleep for six months or more each winter.
